title: refactor(dedicated-autoscaler): separate burst tokenbucket controller + improved utilization reporting
author: Maya Ortega
description: Motivation: the existing Dedicated autoscaler mixes steady-state autoscaling logic and burst tokenbucket controls in a single controller. This made reasoning about burst capacity, telemetry, and rollout policies difficult and caused an incident where tokenbucket state leaked across fleet boundaries. This PR separates the burst tokenbucket into its own controller, standardizes per-fleet utilization metrics, and improves reporting for throughput guarantees. Changes include: 1) extract TokenBucketController responsible for per-fleet burst accounting, rate limiting, and token refill policy; 2) keep AutoscalerController focused on steady-state replica decisions and scaling policies; 3) introduce new metrics (dedicated_fleet_burst_tokens, dedicated_fleet_burst_utilization, dedicated_fleet_throughput_guarantee_satisfied) and expand existing utilization tags to include fleet_id and capacity_tier; 4) add a lightweight in-memory cache with evictions for stale fleet entries to avoid unbounded memory growth; 5) add e2e tests that simulate burst traffic and verify token accounting and fallback policies; 6) update docs and API for configuring burst windows and token refill rates. Migration notes: TokenBucketController will, on first startup post-deploy, reconcile existing burst state from the admin API; there is a short window where historical token accounting is unavailable, but we default to conservative burst allowances during reconciliation. Also added a roll-forward feature flag (feature.dedicated.burst_tokenbucket_v2) to allow staged rollout. Related Linear: ENG-1284 (autoscaler refactor), ENG-1300 (throughput guarantees). Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] e2e tests for burst scenarios, [x] docs updated, [x] migration and feature flag. Impact: no breaking API changes for users; operators should monitor the new metrics after rollout.
commits: Extract TokenBucketController and move burst-specific logic out of AutoscalerController
Add per-fleet metrics and tag enrichment (fleet_id, capacity_tier)
Implement in-memory fleet cache with TTL and eviction
Add e2e test suite simulating concurrent burst traffic and verify fallback policies
Docs: dedicated/README.md add burst configuration and migration notes
Add feature flag and rollout gating in deployment manifests
review_comments: Liam: Can we ensure the TokenBucketController does not introduce cross-fleet contention? Suggests adding per-fleet sharding and lockless counters.
Author (Maya): Added per-fleet sharding and moved heavy ops off the reconciliation loop. See tokenbucket_controller.go lines 120-220 for sharding logic.
Sofia: CI flaked on e2e when simulating high concurrency; looks like test relied on timing. Recommend using deterministic mocks for token refill intervals.
Author (Maya): Updated tests to use a mocked clock and increased timeouts; re-ran e2e, passing now.
Ethan: Metrics look good; please add example Grafana panels to the docs for ops to monitor burst utilization and throughput guarantees.
Author (Maya): Added Grafana snippet to docs/dedicated/burst-controls.md under 'Monitoring'.
release_notes: Improved dedicated autoscaler: separated burst tokenbucket controller, enhanced per-fleet utilization and throughput guarantee reporting, added migration notes and feature flag for staged rollout. Operators: monitor dedicated_fleet_burst_utilization and dedicated_fleet_throughput_guarantee_satisfied after upgrading.
notes_for_release_manager: This is a non-breaking, backwards-compatible refactor. Enable feature.dedicated.burst_tokenbucket_v2 behind the flag by default in canary and monitor metrics for 24-48h before full rollout. If unexpected burst denials are observed, rollback the feature flag to restore previous behavior.
incident_reference: SUP-4021 (tokenbucket state leak incident - root cause: mixed controller state leading to cross-fleet accounting)
